title: INEC To Use Artificial Intelligence To Verify Results In 2027 Elections, Detect Cyberattacks
key_facts: INEC (Nigeria's Independent National Electoral Commission) chairman Prof. Joash Amupitan spoke at a press conference on Tuesday (6 Oct 2026) on preparations for the 2027 general elections.
INEC created an AI Division inside its ICT department.
Automated AI auditing tools are already integrated into result verification under a five-pillar AI governance framework with mandatory human oversight.
An AI governance framework policy is still being finalised.
INEC is working with international technology partners on AI anomaly-detection tools to monitor database traffic and block cyber intrusions and unauthorised changes.
A nationwide mock accreditation exercise is also planned.
Social media users asked what AI would actually do, whether it addresses BVAS (voter accreditation) and result-transmission problems in poor-network areas, and who controls and audits it.
quote_evidence: "Automated AI auditing tools have been integrated into our result verification process under a five-pillar AI governance framework operating under mandatory human oversight."
"An AI governance framework policy is being finalised by the commission."
"AI is only as reliable as the data fed into it," wrote one X user.
why_it_matters_hint: Nigeria's election body says AI will help check results and defend systems, amid public doubt about detail and oversight.
notes: Based on the chairman's statements as reported by one outlet; partner companies not named; scope of AI not specified. Reactions quoted are from individual X users, not representative.
